transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-10
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~75 minutes
Attendees: Liam, Sofia, Devon, Maya, Ethan, Priya, Tom, Janelle

Summary:
Quick alignment on Q4 launch readiness for the new Dedicated scaling changes, review of last week's incident and mitigation, and assignment of final pre-launch tasks. Action items captured and owners assigned.

00:00 - Liam: okay, thanks everyone for joining; we'll run about an hour, hour 15. Quick agenda - roadmap priorities, launch checklist, incident follow-up, and then open items.
00:28 - Priya: sounds good. we need to make sure marketing and support have the playbook, too. not just eng.
00:42 - Sofia: agreed, i'll coordinate the support dry-run. i wanted to flag one thing on the checklist - the rollback policy is still the vague spot.
01:05 - Devon: yeah on the rollback, we had that partial rollback issue in the incident last week where some nodes didn't rejoin cleanly, so the KV cache got out of sync, K-V cash i guess i say it wrong, but that caused read mismatches in the canary.
01:28 - Maya: right, and the SRE runbook had step ordering that confused the automation; we should make the runbook explicit: drain, scale down, clear kv cache, and then scale back up.
01:50 - Tom: also we need to confirm SOC2/ISO checklist for the launch; Compliance is asking for the latest audit logs retention policy and KMS config.
02:12 - Liam: noted - i'll include audit log retention and KMS pointers in the runbook. who will own sending the compliance packet to Legal?
02:28 - Priya: i'll own the packet, but need the config bits from SRE.
02:40 - Maya: i'll pull the KMS and log retention configs and post them to the shared drive. link: (drive/release/launch-configs)
03:05 - Ethan: small item on UX - when we have partial capacity fallback to hosted, we need a clear banner and error states so customers understand degraded mode.
03:30 - Devon: good catch. technically the smart routing already does fallback to hosted variants, but we need the API to carry a reason code so UI can render the banner.
04:00 - Liam: action item there for dev+design to agree on the reason code schema.
04:22 - Sofia: on the performance side, we still have a p95 target of 150ms for short chat flows; during the incident we saw p95 spike to 420 on some models. devon, any root cause?
04:42 - Devon: most of it was batching + kernel selection thrash when the sequence length distribution shifted unexpectedly; the runtime switched a kernel that was fine for longer sequences but bad for short responses. we need a better compile-check on model profiles.
05:20 - Maya: we also saw pod eviction during the spike; autoscaler didn't respond fast enough because the burst policy thresholds are conservative.
05:40 - Tom: can we tighten the autoscale thresholds for the launch window and then revert?
05:55 - Devon: yes, but we should do a 72-hour soak to ensure we don't get noisy neighbors; i'll run a dedicated-host throughput test and a mixed workloads test.
06:20 - Liam: put that in the action items - devon + maya to run the soak and share the spreadsheet of results. link will be inserted in the runbook.
06:40 - Priya: timeline question - are we still aiming for feature flag gated rollout starting 2026-10-01?
06:55 - Liam: tentatively yes. final decision after soak and dry-run scheduled next week.
07:12 - Janelle: QA needs acceptance criteria; can we list regression test prompts and target latencies?
07:30 - Sofia: i'll publish the test harness and the eval prompt set; Jenkins job will run nightly during the soak.
07:50 - Ethan: design will finalize error states and the rollout banner copy by 2026-09-15.
08:05 - Priya: i'll prepare a comms plan only after the dry-run, but i'll need the failure scenarios documented.
08:20 - Lomb: (unclear interjection)
08:30 - Liam: quick incident review recap - root cause was kernel selection + kv cache inconsistency after partial rollback. mitigations: explicit rollback steps, add reason codes to API, tighten autoscale temporarily during launch, run 72-hour soak, and verify KMS/log retention for compliance.
09:02 - Tom: on compliance, do we have an outstanding ask from Legal on data residency? a few enterprise customers want EU-only logs.
09:20 - Maya: we have region log routing but need to call that out in the runbook and confirm with infra.
09:35 - Devon: also need to double-check model variants are pinned in the release so the runtime won't choose a different variant mid-rollout.
09:50 - Liam: ok, we'll pin model versions for the rollout window.
10:05 - Sofia: dry-run plan - SRE + Support + QE will simulate a canary with 5% traffic, then inject latency and then do a rollback. needs to be scheduled next week; preferred date 2026-09-22.
10:30 - Priya: support training note - include the banner reasons and suggested scripts for customers.
10:45 - Ethan: will put suggested copy in the design doc and link to the runbook.
11:10 - Liam: let's capture the top risks: 1) rollback automation not deterministic; 2) autoscaler response slow; 3) compliance packet incomplete; 4) UX confusion on fallback.
11:35 - Priya: can we add a risk owner column in the runbook?
11:45 - Liam: yes, will do.
12:00 - Action review & recap:
- Liam to publish runbook + risk table + audit links (due 9/17)
- Devon + Maya to run soak + perf benchmarks (due 9/24)
- Sofia to schedule dry-run w/ Support & QE (due 9/18)
- Ethan to finalize UI copy (due 9/15)
- Priya to prepare compliance packet after SRE confirms configs (due 9/20)

71:00 - Meeting ends.

Notes on transcript quality: some names and acronyms may be transcribed imperfectly (KV cache/K-V cash, some speaker overlaps), timestamps roughly every 30-90 seconds. References to artifacts: runbook draft (drive/release/launch-configs), perf spreadsheet (sheets/perf/2026-q4-soak), design doc (docs/design/launch-ui).

Recap email bullet to send after meeting: share runbook link, perf soak plan, dry-run calendar invite, and action owners with due dates.

End of transcript.
